architecture_layers.name: Infrastructure & Config

core_dependencies.description: Binary entry point dispatches CLI commands into library modules
core_dependencies.to: src (lib root: cli, config, pipeline, drift, doctor)

core_dependencies.description: CLI parsing and TOML/config merging produce the Config consumed by the pipeline
Preprocess phase: deterministic repo scan produces ScanData/FileEntry inputs
Executes the declarative agent DAG in dependency-level order for Research and Compose
Drives devin/claude/codex/mock backends via the AgentBackend trait and for_kind factory
Write and Verify phases: doc-tree writer, renderers, and post-write verifier
Calls backends with caching, quota accounting, retry, and model fallback
Shared typed ResearchContext for inter-agent results; materials inject scan data into prompts
Agent output contracts: lenient serde/schemars report types for dir_summary, relationships, research
Markdown prompt templates are loaded as data and rendered/injected at runtime; no code-level reference
Deterministic renderers (database, boundary) consume typed research reports
Language detection, sanitizing, and raw import extraction feed edge resolution
Resolves raw imports into Internal/External/Unresolved file edges and builds FileGraph
build_file_graph runs extract_imports then per-language resolvers over every file
Reads LLM-produced core_dependencies claims JSON to compare against the real import graph
Cross-cutting infrastructure services injected into PipelineCtx and the runner
Offline integration tests exercise pipeline via MockBackend and drift via fixture scan targets

key_insights: Clean layered architecture: scanner and drift import extraction are pure/deterministic; all LLM interaction is isolated behind the AgentBackend trait in src/backend.
src/pipeline is the single orchestration hub — it owns PipelineCtx and sequences scanner → agent DAG → output, keeping phases decoupled.
The agent layer uses a declarative spec/registry DAG plus a typed ResearchContext store, so research agents communicate via typed reports rather than direct coupling.
Prompt templates are pure data dependencies (loaded at runtime), so prompt changes carry no compile-time coupling — but also no compile-time validation of template variables.
src/drift forms a self-contained read-only subsystem (imports → resolve → compare/report) that depends on LLM claims only via a JSON file, enabling offline CI gating.
No circular dependencies: dependencies flow strictly upward from scanner/backend/reports into agent and pipeline; drift consumes agent output as data, not code.
Peripheral risk: mock.rs lives in src/backend, meaning test infrastructure is compiled into the production adapter layer; acceptable but worth noting for binary size/separation.
Fixture crates under tests/ are intentionally isolated (own Cargo workspace) and only scanned, so test targets cannot leak into the main dependency graph.
